昨天才看到有DEMO，今天就发售了，不用等真是太好了。 目前为止玩了几个小时，体验不错，完成度蛮高。 轻量化的游戏体验，简单好上手，也不缺卡组、道具搭配的深度。 老少咸宜，没有18+内容，不用担心儿子闺女来GANK。 挺不错的游戏，但貌似没在国内找人推流，要不考虑下BILIBILI找纸片人主播玩一玩？ 毕竟这价位也够低了（相比其他日本游戏厂的定价来说），有官中，相信愿意尝试的人还是不少的。 下面的话是我找人工智障型AI翻的，如有冒犯，一切责任归于AI~ "よーし、貴様らのゲームはなかなか面白いではないか。非常に良い出来栄えだ。" “なかなか面白いゲームと思う、良い出来栄えだ。”
就目前而言，内容量还是偏少的，很容易玩一会就不知道还能干啥了，期待后续更新吧。 不过目前的价位还是能和内容量匹配上的

I wish I had found more reviews... Maybe this will save someone 12 hours of playing a captcha only to find out they hate the actual game. GL! Starts out playing a card game where you kill monsters and can upgrade/deck build which was decent for what it felt like it was. The different deck types were cool. it had an interesting selection of play mechanics and was rather enjoyable to figure out. Then after you get through all that you find out you were playing a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ captcha/anti bot game to get the real game. If I had the real game to begin with I would've uninstalled and asked for a refund. Think Idle slayer without idle and nothing to collect with a double jump mechanic to avoid obstacles. Apparently you must close the game out in order to get back to the card game. That was nice to find out. Still not recommending this.

This game gives no foreshadowing of how much depth it has until you get there. The first run will probably be simple and give the impression of a free itch.io game, but from the third deck forward it gets WAY more interesting. I just wish the first hour of gameplay made this more clear, because I can see people refunding after the first hour, thinking the rest of the game will be repetitive... There's a reason the only negative reviews are saying it's "too hard" and "RNG based". It's genuinely a skill issue...

I found Lethal Dungeon through Olexa's channel. I'm a fan of deck builders, and LG is a very clever twist. The card selection and relics are interesting, the starting decks lead to different gameplay experiences, and the puzzle aspect is challenging. There is a surprising amount of content and the game will keep you occupied for a while. Plus there are several cool gimmicks that caught me off-guard and kept me glued to the screen for much longer than I planned to spend that day! Strongly recommended.

Personally, having beaten this game and also got to a10 in slay the spire 2, if I had to choose between sts2 and this, I would choose this. Compared to sts2, this game focuses on each encounter with the enemies more than the overall gameplan. Each and every battle feels like a lethal puzzle due to the reward system. This game also has an unbelievable depth, when playing it, you have to consider multiple different lines that could lead to totally different outcomes and find the one that spends the least amount of cards, and sometimes, dealing more damage isn’t the best choice. In addition, it is extremely rewarding if you find an alternative sequence that results in you having one more card in your hand at the end. It's insane that such a seemingly small roguelike game requires this amount of thinking and sequencing constantly. There are six starting decks, and the first five scale in complexity exponentially. It's just so well-designed. There are even built-in lethal puzzles. So if you enjoy finding lethal and the most efficient lethal, I would highly recommend this game.

This is less of a deckbuilder and more of a puzzle game. The deckbuilding elements are rather weak: there are limited opportunities to add cards, and runs are limited in time anyway. Rather, the fun comes from figuring out how to work with the limited resources that you have. There are some definite balance issues, with some relics and cards feeling completely useless 99% of the time. But its a nice change of pace from your traditional deckbuilder.

It's the kind of game that I didn't know I wanted. It's personally all the more special to me since someone I really care about showed me this game in the first place. Though even outside of that bias, it's a great experience and definitely worth the price. If you're not sure if you want it, then try the demo. You'll want it after that, all to satisfy the craving of wanting to see everything else that the game offers in the full experience, as well as...something very special after "finishing the game", so to speak. The Perfectly Balanced Combo Kill Card, my beloved.

Honestly, this is just a really fun, solid game. It blends deckbuilding and puzzle mechanics in a way that actually feels like a fresh twist on the usual roguelike formula, rather than just copying what's out there. The balance is good, and the progression doesn't feel cheap. If you’re not sure about dropping the cash, just play the demo first it’s what hooked me, and you'll know pretty quickly if you want the full thing. Finding crazy card combos is a blast, and for the price, it’s absolutely worth it.

Incredibly fun game with really simple instructions, solid mechanics, and creative ideas. Despite being a pretty short game, there were multiple times I gasped or went, "no way, that's so cool." The graphics are really appealing and the sfx/movements feel good (though I would love if the monsters had some movement :') ). Genuinely sooo glad I discovered this game when playing a bunch of random demos a few months ago. The game logic was sound (I don't think I noticed any bugs?), and I never felt like it was unfair (even though the Combine deck was... really tough at higher levels...). (Also: big fan of the hand puppet dog?? It's really such a great vibe and adds kind of a whimsical, silly freak energy. ♡) +Love that there's a puzzle mode! Would love to see more puzzles added. (#17 was a doozy...) Thank you developer for this memorable experience. :')

(No idea if this messes with other progression in some subtle way.)

Smart little card-based RPG with logic puzzle-like gameplay. Traverse a dungeon by winning each battle using a single hand of cards, upgrading cards and unlocking new decks as you progress. By Nihohe.
